chapter: Building the band: Dave Duncan, Denver and Rene Hall
title: Hiring Salva Sanders, Count Basie's early idol
summary: Salva Sanders quits the Southern Serenaders after their pianist falls off the stool drunk, and Fields takes him on.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: See we haven't gotten to the bus yet. So we made that trip and came back in--I'm trying to think who was on my first trip

with me--but anyway, Frenchie Hughes--we called him Frenchie--a young man that I was in Tusko gee with, a saxophone player and Salva Sanders, and believe it or not, if you ever talk to Count, that was Count's idol when he was barn-storming around Tulsa and Oklahoma City. Salva had that little fingering that Count finally perfected and Salva's brother--I'm telling you the truth--
Ron mentioned him in his letter? I don't recall.

Anyway, when the news came in to Tulsa, with the group, when these road guys would go in front and book the band, and Salva came in, I believe, with the Southern Serenaders, but he was originally from (inaudible), Oklahoma and had gone to school out in Langston, university, but had left town and joined the Southern Serenaders, but he came in and then

came in working a black job there and then he couldn't get work and Salva said, I'm not going there, I'm giving up on the Southern Serenaders and so I said Sal (inaudible). So I said I'll try and see what I can.

So then I jumped on Frenchie, the saxophone player and Frenchie said yeah, I don't want to go out anymore depending on a whiskey head. The piano player with the group--I forget what they called him--was--the star was the piano player, and this booker had the guys in some theater, he got them to use this band and they had played good in Muskogee and they came to Tulsa in a theater there and booked them and when the lights went on, this cat fell off the stool--the piano player. I don't remember what his name was.

Anyway, he told the booker, I've had it, I just can't put my job up against a whiskey head, I'm going; that's the man that you're featuring, you don't know what condition he's going to be in; so he left.
